profile.campus: Aurora, Kane/DuPage County, Illinois (CyrusOne CHI3 building)
profile.reading:
Per two independent aggregator listings (datacentermap, datacenterHawk) agreeing on the address, corroborated by CyrusOne's own Aurora campus page, CHI3 sits at 2725 Bilter Road, Aurora, IL, part of the shared 450,000 sq ft / 114MW CHI1-CHI3 campus, distinct from the CHI1/CHI2 buildings on nearby Diehl Road.

CyrusOne acquired the original Aurora CME Group data center (now CHI1) in March 2016 for roughly $130 million, with CME Group continuing to run its Globex matching engine on site under a 15-year lease; CyrusOne was founded in July 2000 by David Ferdman and Larry Bursten and was taken private in 2022 when Kohlberg Kravis Roberts (KKR) and Global Infrastructure Partners (GIP) acquired the company for approximately $15 billion.

Since going private under KKR and GIP ownership in 2022, CyrusOne has continued expanding its US and international footprint; the company's own press materials cite roughly $1 billion in cumulative capital investment in its San Antonio, Texas campuses alone as of a January 2025 groundbreaking, indicating continued growth investment across its portfolio under private ownership rather than a broad slowdown following the take-private transaction.

In November 2021, KKR and GIP first announced the agreement to acquire CyrusOne in an approximately $15 billion transaction, one of the largest data center M&A deals of that period, reflecting broader private-equity and infrastructure-fund interest in colocation real estate that has also driven acquisitions of peers like QTS (by Blackstone) and CoreSite (by American Tower) around the same era; CyrusOne's current published portfolio language describes more than 50 mission-critical facilities worldwide, though the company's own site and Wikipedia give somewhat different approximate totals (over 40 versus more than 50), neither of which this registry treats as a precise, independently verified figure.

reading.body:
CyrusOne CHI3 is a 450,000 square foot data center building in Aurora, Illinois, part of a three-building campus on Bilter Road. The operator has published 114 MW of total IT capacity across the entire Aurora campus, but has not published a figure specific to this building, so its individual contribution to Illinois' data center footprint cannot be calculated from available specifications.

Illinois has 44 mapped data center facilities, of which only 6 operators have published power capacity figures totaling 236 MW. This campus ranks seventh among published capacity figures in the state, though this reflects the three-building Aurora campus aggregate rather than CHI3 alone, and most facilities in Illinois publish no figures at all.

Without a building-specific power figure, the significance of CHI3 to AI scaling cannot be read from its specifications. The 450,000 square feet is consistent with a mid-scale hyperscale building, which at typical AI densities of 40 kW per rack would support roughly 4,500 racks, but this remains an assumption about utilization rather than a fact about the facility's configuration.
